title: Twins’ Joe Ryan to be evaluated for an injury, and his next start is uncertain
content:
KANSAS CITY, Mo. — Minnesota Twins All-Star pitcher Joe Ryan’s next start is in doubt; he is returning home to be evaluated for back and glute issues, the club said Wednesday.

Twins manager Derek Shelton said that Ryan, who has lost three straight starts since the All-Star break, already left the team to be evaluated by team physician Christopher Camp in Minneapolis.

“That’s what we’re trying to figure out,” Shelton said. “He’s frustrated and not able to replicate his delivery. … The ability to repeat his delivery, I’m not going to say it’s not physical. But we owe it to him and to us to find out what he’s feeling and how he’s going about it.”

Ryan spoke cryptically about what he’s experiencing after giving up four earned runs in 5 1/3 innings in Tuesday’s 8-2 loss to the Kansas City Royals. Asked whether he feels physically capable of doing what he wants with his delivery, Ryan said, “No, definitely not.”

Ryan has a 9.39 ERA over his past three outings, allowing 25 hits over 15 1/3 innings. Ryan surrendered a major-league record six home runs in a July 20 road start against the Cleveland Guardians, his first after making his second All-Star Game appearance the week before.

The Twins described Ryan as working through arm fatigue and afforded him extra time after his Cleveland start. He pitched again nine days later, allowing four earned runs in six innings in a home loss to Kansas City.

Shelton said the team believes Ryan’s issues aren’t arm-related but are instead related to his lower body.

Losing Ryan would be a blow to a Twins club hoping to make noise down the stretch after acquiring four pitchers ahead of Monday’s trade deadline.

Ryan was dominant enough in the first half of the season to help the Twins overcome the loss of Pablo López, who tore the ulnar collateral ligament in his right elbow in February and needed season-ending Tommy John surgery.

Ryan posted a 2.85 ERA with 128 strikeouts in 110 1/3 innings, earning him a spot on the All-Star team when squads were announced July 4.

The team appears better prepared to handle an absence from any of its starting pitchers after acquiring starter Dean Kremer from the Baltimore Orioles on Friday. Saying they didn’t want an injury in the rotation to be their “Achilles’ heel,” general manager Jeremy Zoll sought to add starting depth and secured Kremer, who has struggled in seven starts this season but has a 4.37 career ERA over five-plus years in the big leagues.

If the Twins decide to place Ryan on the 15-day injured list, they could recall Zebby Matthews, who was optioned to Triple-A St. Paul on Saturday following a strong start in Seattle, where he struck out 10 batters in five innings against the Mariners. Matthews is 4-8 with a 5.22 ERA in 14 starts this season.
